data.summary: Personal vs project constraints: user preferences recorded as constraints leak into every teammate's prime
data.detail: Colton (2026-09-15): users record personal preferences as constraints, and constraints are project-wide — prime's Active Constraints section shows every constraint to everyone regardless of who recorded it. Needs a personal/project split so a person's preferences apply only to them. Not built in v0.41.0 and no prior plan found in the graph. Per-person journal shards (v0.41.0) store who wrote each entry but the replayed graph is shared, so shards alone do not scope visibility. Open design questions: how scope is marked (field on constraint vs new node type), default for existing constraints, whether personal constraints are visible to teammates in search, how the recording agent decides scope.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Personal constraints rulings (Colton, 2026-09-15): constraints default to personal; teammates cannot find another person's personal constraints; agent judges scope by guidance and asks the human when unsure
data.detail: Personal preferences recorded as constraints were leaking into every teammate's prime and search. Ruling: a constraint defaults to personal (applies only to its recorder, by recorded_by email) unless it is true for anyone in the repo; the tool and skill carry guidance for judging, and the agent asks the human when unsure. Personal constraints are hidden from teammates across prime, search, node/neighbor lookups, dashboard and curation — not merely labeled. Rejected: labeled-but-visible (teammates' agents could still obey them) and a new preference node type. Known limit: hidden through the plugin, but still readable in the owner's committed journal file.

data.summary: Codex gate found two curation defects invisible on Claude Code: an analyzer registered itself on teammate-comms and mailed proposals outside the run, and a transient "agent thread limit reached" spawn refusal had no handling
data.detail: First live Codex exercise of v0.41.0-v0.43.0 (Vince-Codex, 2026-09-17). The conflict analyzer EXPLICITLY called teammate_register (first attempt failed with "Invalid agent name '/root/vibe_curate'", second succeeded) and then mailed its proposals to four addresses including an agent outside the curation run; the orchestrator had received the same JSON through the normal final-answer path, so nothing was lost, but nothing in the analyzer prose forbade any of it. Separately the scope-analyzer spawn was refused with exactly "agent thread limit reached" — a transient concurrency limit our prose never named, unlike the structural "Agent depth limit reached" — and succeeded on a retry after in-flight analyzers finished. Claude Code cannot surface either: its spawn discipline already forbids named spawns and it has no thread limit. Fixed in 0.43.1. Standing lesson: harness-specific spawn surfaces need their own live gate; a green Claude Code run says nothing about Codex.

data.summary: A curation run committed an edge tagged source "curate-edge-analyzer" instead of "curate-skill", tripping the edges_outside_curation smoke detector, and its hand-back reported 0 edges created while an edge had landed
data.detail: Observed 2026-09-17 on Claude Code v0.43.1. The run's final message said "2 uncurated nodes processed -> 0 edges created", but get_status showed edges 1642 -> 1643 and a new edge_sources key "curate-edge-analyzer": 1, with edges_outside_curation rising 85 -> 86. The edge is c4fd8344ad92 -[led_to]-> 9e422742c92f. Cause: the per-edge `source` field is copied from the analyzer's JSON, and the analyzer emitted its own agent name instead of the sanctioned value; the edge-analyzer's documented example uses "source": "curate-skill", and _EDGE_SOURCE_CURATION_EXEMPT in storage.py accepts only deterministic/task-parent/curate-skill/curate-conflict/curate-cluster/curator, so any other string is counted as a write made outside curation. Two defects in one run: wrong provenance on a real edge, and an under-reported count in the hand-back (the same run type that twice returned "placeholder" -- see fail 0d0e0b497d81). Nothing is corrupted: the edge itself is legitimate, only its provenance tag and the count are wrong. Open question for Colton: whether add_edges_batch should reject or normalise an unknown source under a curation token rather than trusting the analyzer's string.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: v0.44.0 built: replay is append-only and a rolled-back journal repairs itself, after two rejected designs and four peer reviewers
data.detail: Violet (vibe-memory) reported that a stale journal file on disk destroyed live nodes on replay: five incidents, 1 to 93 nodes, two unrecoverable. Colton ruled for full append-only replay plus automatic repair of the person's own file, and for two rounds of multi-reviewer review before release. Two designs were rejected in plan review before building: keeping the graph in memory (retention is per-process, so the reported cold-start sequence has no witness; it also splits the graph and blinds the loss detector), and a machine-local mirror of every applied line of every file (legacy positional stamps make a mirror-order union pick a different winner; it surfaces teammates' personal-constraint ids below the visibility choke point; it copies every teammate's content onto every machine; and it gated the read-only escape hatch while leaving the disk-writing heal ungated). Shipped instead: append-only replay, an own-appends ledger written synchronously with each append, retention plus reporting for files this checkout may not write, one locked multi-notice alert read without being deleted, git-aware deliberate-move detection, and an audited accept-disk. Nine blockers/highs from the two post-work rounds were all fixed: an unlocked notices file rewritten on nearly every tool call, accept-disk undercounting what it destroys, a retained notice that self-cleared while the file stayed broken, alerts overwriting each other, an own-file notice blaming a teammate, worktree/submodule branch misdetection, and per-call IO. My own tests caught three bugs during the build: the heal path pruned the ledger (making it useless), opening the store healed before accept-disk could act, and a Windows handle held on a file being replaced made every prune fail silently. Gates: 1729 passed with the 2 pre-existing lifecycle failures, svn 16/16, both perturbations bite. Not claimed: incident 3483de902c18 (mid-curation, no git command) has an unknown mechanism and stays open. Field test in vibe-memory requested from Violet; the pin is held until it reports.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Hermes harness #3 re-evaluation (research only): Hermes stays shelved — upstream rejected scoped delegation, and the "harness #3 is cheaper" infrastructure promise was only half-built
data.detail:
Re-evaluated adding Nous Research Hermes as harness #3 now that Codex ships as harness #2 (requested by Colton 2026-09-21; investigation only, no implementation). Three parallel research tracks: a live re-verification of the 2026-08-31 Hermes findings, an internal audit of the harness-abstraction layer, and a survey of alternative harness candidates. Written up in docs/hermes-reevaluation-2026-09-21.md.

RECOMMENDATION: do not adopt Hermes now. Do the harness-agnostic hardening first (Phase A); if a third harness is still wanted, Hermes is not the strongest candidate.

Hermes side: all five 2026-08-31 findings held up. Two improved materially in our favour — shell-script hooks (not just a native Python plugin) can return {"context": ...} on pre_llm_call, which is the shape our injection path already has; and Windows is now documented as first-class native with a bundled portable Git Bash, removing a risk the plan rated high. Two got worse — plugin and shell hook registration is reported broken under `hermes serve`/desktop (two open issues), so injection would silently no-op there; and the decisive one, per-spawn model pinning and per-spawn tool scoping for delegate_task, is not a backlog gap but a rejected feature (issues #9459/#35409 closed, PR #48644 closed unmerged, maintainer "We do not want this"). That makes curation containment and model tiering permanently partial on Hermes rather than a burndown item that clears.

Our side: containment (WP-H0a) and dependency bootstrap generalize cleanly and a third harness inherits them free. But the conformance kit (WP-H0c) and docs/harness-contract.md (WP-H0b) were never built, the renderer is hardcoded to exactly two harnesses, and a third of the policy table is dead. So "harness #3 cheaper than harness #2" currently holds only for containment and bootstrap.

Also found: Agent Plugins v1 is now a governed standard (steering committee of Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel, Google) with Anthropic outside it; our packaging bet looks good but no longer depends on Hermes. Gemini CLI and opencode both offer per-subagent model pins plus tool allowlists natively, which is exactly what Hermes refuses to build.

Evidence caveat (ledger 23): nobody has Hermes installed; every Hermes claim is doc- or source-derived and must be spiked live before any brief. Adoption figures returned by the research pass were implausibly large and are flagged as needing hand-checking.

data.summary: The harness renderer silently renders EMPTY content for any harness with no matching block — 50 blocks (35 in curate-orchestrator) would vanish for harness #3, and no test catches it
data.detail:
Found while re-evaluating Hermes as harness #3 (docs/hermes-reevaluation-2026-09-21.md). tools/render_harness.py's block substitution in render_text() returns the block body only when the block's harness name equals the harness being rendered, and an empty string otherwise. There is no branch for "this harness has no block here" — an unmatched harness gets silence, not an error.

Verified counts at HEAD b7d62eb: 50 harness block openings and 50 closings across 7 source files — agents-src/curate-orchestrator.md has 35 of them (16 claude-code, 19 codex), the four analyzer agents have 2 each, skills-src/vibe-curate/SKILL.md has 4, skills-src/vibe-backfill/SKILL.md has 3.

Why the existing tests do not catch it: test_harness_render.py's token test only asserts no leftover "{{" or "}}" markers survive, which an empty render satisfies perfectly. The forbidden-literal lint scans SOURCES, not outputs. The orphan lint checks that every output directory traces back to a source, not that outputs have content.

Consequence: adding harness #3 to the policy table and the renderer without also hand-authoring a matching block at all 50 sites produces a rendered curation orchestrator missing most of its spawn and orchestration instructions, with green CI. This is the same failure class as ledger 12/20 (a green check that does not bind) and it is a defect today, not only a future-harness concern — it is the mechanism that would make the largest authoring task in a harness port fail silently rather than loudly.

Suggested fix direction (not implemented, no authorization): make render_text raise when a source contains harness blocks but none matches the harness being rendered, or require an explicit empty-block opt-in; and add a semantic assertion comparing rendered output size per harness.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Hermes upstream REJECTED per-spawn model pinning and tool scoping for delegate_task — a durable platform position, not a backlog gap, so curation parity on Hermes could never clear
data.detail:
The 2026-08-31 Hermes scoping (episode d82978200b66) recorded that delegate_task has no per-spawn toolsets or model parameter and cited open feature requests #9459 and #35409, framing it as something that might land upstream and simplify the port. Re-verified 2026-09-21: both issues are now CLOSED, and a working implementation (PR #48644, a profile parameter for cross-profile subagents with fail-closed credentials and toolset bounding) was closed UNMERGED on 2026-07-14, with the maintainer commenting "We do not want this" on both issues.

The capability exists in Hermes's internal plumbing — delegate_task()/_build_child_agent() accept model and toolsets — but it is deliberately withheld from the model-facing schema and stripped from anything the LLM supplies. Children inherit the parent model unless pinned by a single global delegation.model in config.yaml.

Why this matters more than it looks: on Codex the equivalent limitation (spawn depth defaulting to 1) was a DEFAULT we designed around with a flat orchestrator plus adaptive fan-out, and users could raise it. On Hermes the limitation is the vendor's stated intent, so the analyzer tiering and per-agent containment that Claude Code gets would be permanently partial — a parity row that can never go full, not a burndown item.

Evidence class: source and issue reads by a research pass, not a live call (ledger 23). Nobody on this team has Hermes installed. Before any Hermes work package, re-check whether the maintainer position has moved.

data.summary: Renderer silently drops harness-block content for any unmatched harness (50 blocks, 35 in curate-orchestrator) — make it fail loudly and add a size-based semantic assertion

data.summary: Hermes upstream REJECTED per-spawn model pinning for delegate_task — a durable platform position that forecloses model TIERING on Hermes (containment is unaffected: it is server-side)
data.detail:
CORRECTED 2026-09-21 after adversarial review caught an overreach in the first version of this node, which claimed curation parity "could never clear" on Hermes. That conflated two different things.

The 2026-08-31 Hermes scoping (episode d82978200b66) recorded that delegate_task has no per-spawn toolsets or model parameter and cited open feature requests #9459 and #35409, framing it as something that might land upstream. Re-verified 2026-09-21: both issues are CLOSED, and a working implementation (PR #48644, a profile parameter with fail-closed credentials and toolset bounding) was closed UNMERGED on 2026-07-14, with the maintainer commenting "We do not want this" on both. The capability exists in Hermes's internal plumbing but is deliberately withheld from the model-facing schema.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COST US: containment. The curation token is server-side and depends on no harness capability. Codex already has no per-agent tool scoping — harness.py records its containment as "curation-session token only (Codex roles cannot restrict tools)" — and all four Codex curation agents are recorded `full` in PARITY.md. A harness without tool scoping reaches full containment parity, and Hermes would.

WHAT IT DOES COST US: model tiering, permanently. Our standing rule since fail f09e770da046 is that every analyzer spawn carries an EXPLICIT model argument because an implicit pin was observed not to hold. Codex satisfies it — each spawn_agent call takes a model, and the orchestrator template states that explicit argument is the only pin there. Hermes has no per-call model at all: children inherit the parent, or a single global delegation.model in the user's config.yaml. So the rule is unsatisfiable per spawn, the only lever is a user config file we neither control nor can guarantee, and orchestrator and analyzers cannot run at different tiers. The cheap mid-orchestrator / small-analyzer fan-out is unavailable.

That is a permanent cost gap, not a safety gap — real, unclearable, but on its own not sufficient grounds to reject Hermes. Evidence class: source and issue reads by a research pass, not a live call (ledger 23); nobody has Hermes installed.

Lesson worth carrying: "harness X lacks per-agent tool scoping" does NOT imply weak containment for this product, because containment was deliberately moved server-side. Check which layer a harness limitation actually lands on before calling it a blocker.

Re-evaluated adding Nous Research Hermes as harness #3 now that Codex ships as harness #2 (requested by Colton 2026-09-21; investigation only, no implementation). Three parallel research tracks plus an adversarial review: a live re-verification of the 2026-08-31 Hermes findings, an internal audit of the harness-abstraction layer, a survey of alternative harness candidates, and a sonnet peer review of the resulting document. Written up in docs/hermes-reevaluation-2026-09-21.md (rev 2, APPROVE-WITH-CHANGES, all nine review findings applied).

RECOMMENDATION: do not adopt Hermes now. Fix the live defects the Codex port left behind; if a third harness is still wanted, spike a candidate rather than resuming the shelved plan.

The recommendation rests on two reasons the review found independently sufficient: (1) the infrastructure that was supposed to make harness #3 cheap was never built — the conformance kit (WP-H0c) and docs/harness-contract.md (WP-H0b) do not exist, so a third harness still writes a conformance suite, a manifest test, a render-test set, and ~50 hand-authored prose blocks; (2) parity on harness #2 is already unpaid at 11 full / 43 partial of 54 rows, with three releases shipping before the last Codex field gate, which then found two real defects.

Hermes side: all five 2026-08-31 findings held. Two improved in our favour — shell-script hooks (not only a native Python plugin) can return {"context": ...} on pre_llm_call, matching the shape our injection path already has, and Windows is now documented as first-class native with a bundled portable Git Bash. Two got worse — hook registration is reported broken under `hermes serve`/desktop, and per-spawn model pinning for delegate_task is a rejected feature upstream (PR #48644 closed unmerged, maintainer "We do not want this").

IMPORTANT CORRECTION made during review: the first draft called that rejection a containment blocker. It is not. Containment is server-side and harness-independent; Codex also lacks per-agent tool scoping and still reached full on all four curation agents. What Hermes forecloses is model TIERING — no per-call model parameter exists, only a global delegation.model in the user's config, so our standing explicit-pin rule (fail f09e770da046) is unsatisfiable per spawn and the cheap mid-orchestrator / small-analyzer split is unavailable. A permanent cost gap, not a safety gap, and not sufficient on its own to reject Hermes.

Also found: Agent Plugins v1 is now a governed standard (steering committee of Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel, Google) with Anthropic outside it; our packaging bet looks good but no longer depends on Hermes. Gemini CLI and opencode are reported to offer per-subagent model pins plus tool allowlists, but that evidence is documentation-level only against primary evidence for Hermes's weakness, so they are a shortlist for spiking, not an earned ranking.

Verified live defects filed or noted: the renderer silently renders empty content for any unmatched harness (task 8a7b6a83e3e9); tests/test_containment_gate.py does not scan adapters/, so the shipped Codex hook scripts are unscanned today; WP-P4 was never filed as a task. Inert-but-trap: update_check.py and whats_new.py read literal CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and silently return 0 when unset, masked today only because the Codex hook sets the Claude-named variables.

Evidence caveat (ledger 23): nobody has Hermes installed; every Hermes claim is doc- or source-derived and must be spiked live before any brief. Adoption figures returned by the research pass were implausibly large and are flagged as needing hand-checking.

data.summary: Before calling a harness limitation a blocker, check WHICH LAYER it lands on — a capability we deliberately moved server-side is not lost when a harness lacks it
data.detail:
Surfaced by the adversarial review of the Hermes re-evaluation (2026-09-21), which caught the first draft claiming that Hermes's lack of per-spawn tool scoping made curation containment permanently partial there.

The reasoning error: "harness X cannot restrict a subagent's tools" reads like a containment blocker, and would have been one under the original Claude-Code-shaped design where the subagent tool whitelist WAS the boundary. But WP-P1 deliberately moved containment into the server as a curation-session token precisely so it would not depend on a harness capability. Codex is the proof: harness.py records its containment as "curation-session token only (Codex roles cannot restrict tools)", and all four Codex curation agents are nonetheless recorded full. The document was measuring Hermes against an architecture we had already replaced.

The general shape: when a portability layer is built specifically to absorb a class of harness variation, findings about that class stop being blockers — but the old mental model persists and keeps re-flagging them. The check is mechanical. For each harness limitation, name the layer that actually implements the affected capability today, then ask whether that layer is ours or the harness's. Ours means the limitation is absorbed; the harness's means it is a real gap.

Adjacent instance in the same review: the correct Hermes finding was a different layer entirely — model TIERING, which genuinely lives in the harness's spawn call and which Hermes does not offer per call. Same research pass, two limitations that look alike, opposite verdicts, and only the layer question separates them.

Relates to ledger 22 (inventory who relies on the current behaviour before changing it) in mirror image: here, inventory what still relies on the harness before declaring a harness gap fatal.

data.summary: Ling Lang MCP server keeps disconnecting because its ChromaDB HNSW files are corrupt, and chromadb's Rust count() then crashes the whole process natively (access violation) during startup
data.detail:
Symptom (2026-09-30, linglang-teacher, v0.44.0): the server exits silently about 3 seconds into startup, twice per connect attempt, and Claude Code reports CONNECTION_CLOSED. The stderr breadcrumbs stop at chroma_open_done. There is no Python traceback and no [vibe-lifecycle] exit line, so the self-exit watchdogs are ruled out.

Reproduced on a COPY of the store at plugins/data/vibe-cognition-coltondyck/chromadb/linglang-teacher-6561fd4b6196, using a standalone script with faulthandler: collection.count() dies with "Windows fatal exception: access violation" in chromadb/api/rust.py _count (chromadb 1.5.5). That is the same call server.py makes in its WP-Wedge-2 pre-exercise, before the watches are armed. With the HNSW segment directory moved aside, the same call raises a normal Python InternalError ("Error finding id") instead of crashing, so the HNSW files are the trigger. SQLite integrity_check is ok.

The corruption signature: every healthy store persists its HNSW in sync_threshold batches of 1000 (vibe-memory has 1000 elements at max_seq_id 1000; Enhanced_Nav has 3000 at 3000). Ling Lang's index was persisted at 3356 elements with max_seq_id 4175, off the batch boundary. The files were last written 2026-09-24 21:33, and the log backlog holds 170 upserts (seq 4175 to 4344). An off-boundary persist means some other writer flushed the shared files.

Most likely cause: several vibe-cognition server processes for the same project share one persist_directory. That sharing is by design since WP-A (decision 9022f7de94e9), and Ling Lang runs the most concurrent sessions. Each process keeps its own in-memory HNSW index and persists it to the same files. chromadb's Rust backend arbitrates SQLite locking across processes, but nothing arbitrates the HNSW files. Earlier "hnsw Nothing found on disk" test flakes (task 7ec1e5929309) are probably the same seam.

Consequence: this is a hard crash that bypasses every try/except. A retry cannot fix it, and the server cannot even report it.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.reason: Discovery states the earlier hnsw 'Nothing found on disk' flakes in this task are probably the same shared-HNSW-files seam.
The WP-A concurrency design that shares one persist_directory across server processes is named as the likely cause of the HNSW corruption crash.

data.summary: Colton ruling (2026-09-30): quarantine Ling Lang's corrupt ChromaDB store now, then plan a crash-proof startup store check (2) plus replacing ChromaDB's HNSW index with SQLite-stored vectors and brute-force search (3a), peer-reviewed before any code
data.detail:
Follows discovery d603acc95c54: a corrupt HNSW index crashes the server natively on startup in Ling Lang.

CHOSEN, in three parts:
(1) Unblock now. With all Ling Lang sessions closed, rename (never delete) the linglang-teacher store folder, so the server builds a fresh store and re-embeds from the journal.
(2) Plan a startup check that probes the store in a throwaway child process. If the child crashes, the server quarantines the store, rebuilds it, and surfaces a prime notice, so one bad store can never take the server down silently.
(3a) Plan to replace ChromaDB's HNSW persistence with vectors stored in SQLite, which is safe with several processes, searched by brute force. That is milliseconds at our scale of about 3-4k vectors x 768 dimensions. It removes both the native-crash dependency and the unarbitrated shared HNSW files.

REJECTED:
(3b) Keep ChromaDB behind a cross-process single-writer lock. It adds another lock and lifecycle seam in the historically most fragile area.
(3c) One shared embedding service per project. Largest lifecycle change.
Unblock-only. Leaves the recurrence open for any project with parallel sessions.

The plan gets a sonnet peer review before implementation.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Curate-orchestrator (v0.44.0) spawned its edge and conflict analyzers in the background despite the foreground-only spawn rule; their results never came back, and it wrote the edges from its own search instead
data.detail:
Observed 2026-09-30 in the vibe-cognition project. The run curated 1 node (d603acc95c54) with 2 edges. Its hand-back says: "The edge and conflict analyzers ran in the background and their results never came back, so I wrote the edges myself from my own search instead."

The launch skill documents the orchestrator's analyzer spawns as foreground-only (SPAWN DISCIPLINE). Two problems follow:
(a) The spawn discipline is not holding.
(b) The fallback bypassed the propose-then-review separation, so the orchestrator acted as both proposer and reviewer.

The small batch meant little harm this time. On a large batch it would silently degrade edge quality. Needs a look at the orchestrator prompt's spawn instructions and at whether background spawning is harness-forced.

data.reason: Discovery of the corrupt HNSW index crashing the server at startup directly motivated the ruling to quarantine the store, add a startup probe, and replace HNSW with SQLite vectors.
Fail shows the orchestrator bypassing propose-then-review containment by writing edges itself after analyzers ran in background.
Fail exposes a defect in the implementation of the background-curation design: analyzer spawn discipline not holding.

data.summary: Colton ruling (2026-10-05): do NOT move the vector store to SQLite. The real fix for multi-process store safety is making vibe-cognition a hosted service, which will be a separate project. This supersedes part 3a of decision fab50df0d13c
data.detail:
After weighing the risks and rewards of replacing ChromaDB's HNSW persistence with SQLite-stored vectors plus brute-force search (plan rev 2, docs/wp-vector-store-plan.md Part A), Colton decided against it. A hosted vibe-cognition service is the intended long-term answer to many server processes sharing one local store. That is a separate future project, so a SQLite migration now would be throwaway work.

Consequences:
- Part A of the rev 2 plan (WP-VectorStore) is shelved, not implemented.
- ChromaDB stays, so the corruption and native-crash risk from discovery d603acc95c54 remains until the hosted service exists.
- Interim protection on ChromaDB (for example, a startup check that probes the store in a throwaway child process and auto-quarantines it, from the original "part 2") is still open, pending Colton's scoping.
- Part B (WP-CurateAsync, curation analyzers arriving asynchronously) is unaffected by this ruling.

The rev 2 Part A review findings remain useful prior art for the hosted-service design: error classification (busy vs corrupt), whole-directory quarantine under a lock, the rebuild lease to avoid N-session re-embed storms, the venv-guard and hook couplings to chromadb, and the subprocess-test data-root leak.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: A child-process ChromaDB probe detects the Ling Lang corruption reliably: the crash surfaces as returncode 0xC0000005 through the plugin venv's python.exe launcher, and the probe costs about 2 s, most of it chromadb import
data.detail:
Measured 2026-10-05 on Colton's machine, for WP-ChromaGuard (docs/wp-chroma-guard-plan.md).

The probe is a child Python that opens PersistentClient, runs get_collection, count, a filtered get, then get(limit=1) and query. Launched with subprocess.run from the plugin venv's Scripts/python.exe, it returns 3221225477 (0xC0000005, access violation) on a copy of the corrupt linglang-teacher store, in 1.83 s. The venv python.exe is a ~255 KB launcher that starts the base Store Python as a child, and it passes the crash code through intact. Git Bash shows the same crash as exit 139; that is shell translation, not the real code.

Cost:
- Healthy stores (1.7k and 3.7k vectors) take 1.95 to 2.17 s; a bare interpreter starts in 0.2 s.
- The server's own module import already spends most of its ~2.5 s in _venv_guard, which really imports chromadb at import time (REAL_IMPORT_MODULES).
- So a probe spawned between _startup_timing and _venv_guard overlaps almost entirely. Spawned after _venv_guard, it would hide only about 0.7 s.

Other review-confirmed facts for the stopgap design:
- The sidecar supervisor clears embedding_error and sets embedding_ready when the model loads (sidecar_client.py:372,380). Those flags therefore cannot carry a degraded vector-store state, which needs its own context field.
- A kill() on timeout would hit only the launcher and orphan the real interpreter, which still holds the store, so the whole process tree must be killed.
- NTSTATUS codes such as 0xC000013A (Ctrl-C/close) and 0xC0000142 (DLL init) are not corruption. Crash classification must use an allowlist.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: ROOT CAUSE of curation analyzers "being backgrounded despite foreground instructions": Claude Code v2.1.232+ interactive sessions run in fork mode, which removes the Agent tool's run_in_background parameter and makes EVERY spawn async — the orchestrator's SPAWN DISCIPLINE rule 3 ("never end your turn to wait; results arrive in the same tool result") is now false and causes it to hand back self-judged edges before analyzer results arrive
data.detail:
Investigated 2026-10-05 after Lenny (linglang-x-vibememory tenant) reported three /vibe-curate runs on plugin v0.44.0 where the orchestrator said its analyzer spawns "returned async" and it committed edges on its own judgement, skipping the conflict and cluster passes while still reporting success and uncurated=0.

MECHANISM (verified against official docs code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents and the Claude Code CHANGELOG): CHANGELOG 2.1.232: "non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions now run in the background by default". Docs: "Where fork mode is on, as it is by default in an interactive session, Claude Code runs the subagent in the background, forks and non-fork subagents alike, and Claude can't ask for the foreground... Claude Code also removes the Agent tool's run_in_background parameter." Docs on nesting: "In an interactive session... a subagent that launches background subagents waits for their results before it finishes." So the harness DOES route the child result back to the orchestrator, as a later agent-message plus task-notification, and holds the orchestrator's own completion until its children finish. The Agent tool schema in a live 2.1.289 session confirms: no run_in_background parameter; description says "Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes."

EVIDENCE FROM TRANSCRIPTS (~/.claude/projects, all curate-orchestrator subagent transcripts on this machine, 2026-08-30 to 2026-10-05, CC 2.1.250 through 2.1.286): every analyzer Agent call returned "Async agent launched successfully"; zero returned analyzer JSON inline. This has been the behaviour since at least 2.1.250 (before v0.34.0's SPAWN DISCIPLINE rule was even written), so the rule was authored against a world that had already changed. Timeline of a typical Lenny run (agent a6f4785b3d5d6b7dd, 2.1.284): 20:41:49 spawn edge analyzer -> async; 20:41:51-20:42:07 orchestrator does its own neighbor/search review, commits 5 edges itself, marks 4 nodes curated; 20:42:10 SubagentHandback with bare counts (launcher receives THIS); 20:44:44 edge analyzer's report arrives as an agent-message (2 proposed relates_to edges); 20:44:46 task-notification; orchestrator writes "already handled, nothing new" — a message nobody receives. Same shape in the Sep 30 run in vibe-cognition itself on 2.1.286 (agent aef2cbb46b372defd: "I didn't commit the two proposed relates_to edges from the edge analyzer's late report... my earlier handback stands").

CONSEQUENCES: (1) analyzer tokens (~40k per analyzer) are spent and the results discarded every run; (2) edges land on the mid-model orchestrator's own judgement with no propose/review split, contrary to the WP-Curate-Background design; (3) conflict, scope and cluster passes are usually skipped; (4) the run reports success and uncurated hits 0, so nothing surfaces the degradation — Lenny's own transcripts were the only signal. The "embedded analyzer protocol" degraded fallback (meant for a missing Agent tool) is what makes this silent: the orchestrator treats "spawn returned async" as "degraded mode" and proceeds inline.

WHAT IS NOT THE CAUSE: not a named spawn (no `name` passed in any run — the v0.34.0 fix held), not the plugin version, not Windows, not the launching session's run_in_background:true, not the model pin (haiku/sonnet pins were honoured).

FIX DIRECTIONS (not implemented, Colton to rule): (a) rewrite SPAWN DISCIPLINE for fork mode: spawn the analyzers, then END THE TURN WITHOUT calling SubagentHandback; the harness holds the orchestrator open, delivers each analyzer's report as an agent-message, and the orchestrator continues with review/commit and hands back only at the very end. Needs live verification that a parent that stops with live children is held (my own session's task-notification text states "fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own", and the docs say the same). (b) Make the fallback fail loudly instead of self-judging: if an analyzer result is not in hand when review would start, do NOT commit edges or mark curated; report "analyzer results unavailable, re-run /vibe-curate". (c) Harness-level levers exist but are user-global and NOT suitable for a plugin to set: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 (also kills background Bash) or CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 (turns off fork mode for the whole session). (d) Codex path is unaffected: it already uses wait_agent on a returned task path. Non-interactive -p / SDK: docs say the launching subagent does NOT wait there, so (a) needs a -p caveat; 2.1.285 made nested Agent calls foreground under -p with FORK_SUBAGENT=1.
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Why the async-analyzer problem went from harmless to damaging: before Claude Code 2.1.271 the orchestrator simply ended its turn ("I'll continue once it reports back"), the harness fed it the analyzer notification, and its LAST text was the handback; from 2.1.271 the explicit SubagentHandback tool ("call it, then stop") lets the orchestrator finalize before results arrive — early-handback rate rose from 0% (2.1.250-270) to ~10% (2.1.272-283) to 50-86% (2.1.284-288)
data.detail: Classified all 704 curate-orchestrator transcripts on this machine (2026-08-30 to 2026-10-05) by whether the orchestrator's handback (SubagentHandback call, or final text where that tool did not exist) came before or after its first analyzer result arrived. Results: 585 runs got results before handing back, 95 handed back before results, 8 never received a result, 16 spawned nothing (0 uncurated). Per version: 2.1.250-2.1.270 (0 of ~370 early); 2.1.272-2.1.283 (about 18 of ~190 early); 2.1.284 15 of 30, 2.1.286 24 of 28, 2.1.287 18 of 28, 2.1.288 18 of 26, 2.1.289 1 of 4. SubagentHandback first appears in orchestrator transcripts at exactly 2.1.271 (0 of 311 runs before, 100% of runs from 2.1.271 on). The 2.1.284 jump is a correlation only; the per-spawn Agent tool result text ("You know nothing about its results until that notification arrives... continue other work") and the system-reminder "call SubagentHandback and then stop; plain text at the end is not delivered" both push a model that has been told "never end your turn to wait" toward finishing early. A pre-2.1.271 sample run (colton-claude-plugins, 2.1.263) shows the accidentally-correct pattern: spawn edge analyzer, end turn with "running in the background; I'll continue once it reports back", notification arrives ~90s later, commit, spawn conflict analyzer, end turn again, and so on, finishing with the bare-counts line. That is the protocol the fix should make deliberate (ledger rule 10: accidental correctness is an unverified dependency).
data.author: Colton Dyck

data.summary: Colton ruling (2026-10-05): fix the fork-mode curation failure inside the plugin prose (orchestrator ends its turn without SubagentHandback and resumes on each analyzer report; no commit before a report is in hand; fail loudly instead of self-judging) — REJECTED asking users to set global Claude Code env (CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1)
data.detail:
Chosen: rewrite agents-src/curate-orchestrator.md SPAWN DISCIPLINE (Claude Code harness block) and skills-src/vibe-curate/SKILL.md step 3 so the protocol matches fork mode: spawn with no name and no run_in_background; if the spawn result says the analyzer launched in the background, end the turn with a one-line note and no handback; the harness resumes the orchestrator with the report; review and commit only then; SubagentHandback only once, last. Verified live on Claude Code 2.1.289 (agent a9865f96c5e78d276) and by every pre-2.1.271 run on this machine. Where the Agent tool still offers run_in_background (headless -p / SDK, fork mode off), pass run_in_background: false so the result returns inline. Also chosen: an asynchronous launch is explicitly NOT the degraded/no-nesting fallback; the embedded inline protocol is reserved for an absent Agent tool or a tool-not-found / depth-limit error; a batch whose report never arrives is left uncommitted and unmarked with a "re-run /vibe-curate" failure report.

Rejected: (1) telling users to set CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 — Colton's explicit ruling: the plugin does not ask users to change global Claude Code settings; both also change behaviour for everything else in the session (the second kills background Bash). (2) Having the plugin's SessionStart hook set those env vars — same objection, and it would silently alter the user's whole session. (3) Keeping the self-judged fallback as "better than nothing" — it defeats the propose/review split the pipeline exists for and hides the failure behind a success report. Process: solo mode, sonnet peer review of the plan before implementation and of the diff before release, live verification of the new orchestrator text via an inline general-purpose spawn because the installed agent registry is frozen at session start.

data.summary: Re-review path for nodes curated on the orchestrator's own judgement (no un-mark tool exists): nodes marked curated by fork-mode-affected runs (Claude Code 2.1.271 to v0.44.0 plugin) never had analyzer review and cannot be re-queued
data.detail: Found while fixing the fork-mode curation failure (decision 29208ade72c8, discovery 42a3539414d0). Roughly 95 orchestrator runs on this machine alone handed back before their analyzer reports arrived and committed edges on the mid-model orchestrator's judgement, then marked the batch curated. Those edges are not wrong by construction, but they skipped the propose/review split, and the conflict, scope and cluster passes were usually skipped for those nodes. There is no tool to clear curated_by_skill_at or otherwise re-queue a node for curation. Options to evaluate: (a) a curation-gated cognition_requeue_curation(node_ids) tool (curation_token required, audit record appended); (b) a one-shot CLI that requeues every node whose curated_by_skill_at falls inside a given curation_session; (c) accept and let later recordings re-link them naturally. Out of scope for v0.45.0; needs a ruling on whether retroactive re-review is worth the tokens.

data.summary: tests/test_lifecycle_stage1.py::test_supervisor_resolution_against_real_self fails on a Microsoft Store Python (image name python3.13.exe); the assertion only accepts python.exe / pythonw.exe
data.detail: Seen 2026-10-05 on Colton's machine while gating v0.45.0 (unrelated to that release; the failure depends only on the interpreter image name). lifecycle.log_supervisor_identity() resolves verdict=ok and supervisor_image=C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\PythonSoftwareFoundation.Python.3.13_...\python3.13.exe, but the test asserts the lowercased image ends with ("python.exe", "pythonw.exe"). Fix: accept a python3.N(.exe) image name too (regex like python(\d+(\.\d+)?)?w?\.exe), or compare against sys.executable's basename. Check whether lifecycle's own supervisor-image checks (not just the test) have the same assumption; if they do, that is a real bug on Store Pythons, not a test nit.
